Gaming and Leisure Properties, Inc. was established on February 13th, 2013, incorporated in 2013 in Pennsylvania in and is based in Wyomissing, United States.

financial_summary: Gaming and Leisure Properties,  is a large-cap real estate business with a $11.8B market cap on $1.6B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +7% over the past three years and +11% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size. Operating margins are expanding by +4.2pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 10% against a 7% cost of capital, a 4-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $825M in free cash flow — roughly 52 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.37× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 4.9× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and interest coverage runs at 3.2×.

Management returns a meaningful 7.4% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 4.0% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 3.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
